question: Does a logged, rerunnable replication of Card's college-proximity paper (NBER Working Paper 4483, 1993; published 1995 in the Vanderkamp volume, University of Toronto Press, pp. 201-222) from his public NLS Young Men extract (nls.dat) reproduce the published OLS and instrumental-variables estimates of the return to a year of schooling, with proximity to a four-year college in 1966 (nearc4) as the instrument for completed education; and, in the one-endogenous-regressor counterparts of the basic specification (experience treated as exogenous, Table 3 Panel A columns 6 and 5), how much of the IV conclusion survives inference that is robust to a weak instrument and to a bounded violation of the exclusion restriction? The basic three-endogenous-regressor estimate itself (Panel B column 6) is replicated but not given weak-instrument-robust inference. This is a replication: the estimates are published and were exactly reproduced by Kling (2001), and these data have been reanalysed many times since; the paper claims no new finding about the return to schooling. (The seed task and Card's codebook cite NBER WP 4832; the Scout verified that the proximity paper is WP 4483.)
hypotheses: H1 (computational reproduction; targets verified by the Scout from the WP 4483 table images, sources/notes.md sec. 1): N = 3,010 men with a non-missing lwage76, unweighted. Primary target, Card's basic specification (Table 3 Panel B: experience and its square endogenous, instrumented by age and age squared; basic controls plus the 14 family-background variables): 2SLS return 0.132 (s.e. 0.049) in column 6 [claims iv-return, iv-return-se], first-stage coefficient on nearc4 0.365 (0.105) in column 2 [first-stage], reduced form 0.048 (0.019) in column 4; OLS 0.073 (0.004) from Table 2 column 5 [ols-return]. Secondary targets: Table 3 Panel A column 6 (experience exogenous, family background included): 2SLS 0.140 (0.055), first stage 0.322 (0.083), reduced form 0.045 (0.018), OLS Table 2 column 5; Panel A column 5 (no family background): 2SLS 0.132 (0.055), first stage 0.320 (0.088), OLS 0.075 (0.003) from Table 2 column 2, and the homoskedastic Anderson-Rubin 95% set [0.025, 0.285] that Cinelli and Hazlett (2025, Table 2) report for this column. Comparison uses conventional (homoskedastic) standard errors, because the published formula is not stated and the printed 0.055 matches a conventional figure; heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors are reported alongside. Each printed number is reproduced if the replicated value rounds to it at the printed precision (|replicated - published| < half a unit in the last printed digit); N must match exactly. Kling (2001) printed the OLS standard error as .003 where Card printed .004, so that one value may sit on a rounding boundary; the replicated value is reported to four decimals. A failure is reported and diagnosed (sample rule, variable construction, standard-error formula), not tuned away. A pass is a computational check, not new evidence about the return to schooling.

H2 (instrument strength; primary specification Panel A column 6, the one-endogenous-regressor specification that keeps Card's family-background controls; Panel A column 5 reported alongside for comparison with the published literature): the conventional first-stage F on nearc4 is compared with the Stock-Yogo 10% maximal-size critical value for one instrument and one endogenous regressor (16.38), and the Montiel Olea-Pflueger effective F (with one instrument, the heteroskedasticity-robust first-stage F) with its 5%-size, 10%-worst-case-bias critical value (23.11). Each reported as above or below its threshold. The published first-stage t statistics (0.322/0.083 = 3.9; 0.320/0.088 = 3.6) imply F of about 15 and 13, so 'below' is expected and the hypothesis is mainly a check on the robust version; the result changes no specification. Neither threshold applies to the three-endogenous Panel B specification, for which no weak-instrument test is reported; that limit is stated.

H3 (weak-instrument-robust inference; primary Panel A column 6, Panel A column 5 alongside): the heteroskedasticity-robust Anderson-Rubin 95% confidence set for the return to schooling. Decision rule fixed now: 'the IV return to schooling is positive' survives if the robust AR set excludes 0. With one instrument this is the same test as the heteroskedasticity-robust t test of the reduced-form coefficient on nearc4, and the paper says so; the new content is the robust set's bounds on the preferred specification, compared with the homoskedastic set Cinelli and Hazlett (2025) report for column 5. A wide or unbounded set is reported with its bounds, not read as evidence of no return.

H4 (exclusion-restriction sensitivity, descriptive; primary Panel A column 6, column 5 alongside): Conley, Hansen and Rossi (2012) union-of-confidence-intervals with a direct effect gamma of nearc4 on log wages in [0, delta], built from Anderson-Rubin tests (so it is robust to a weak instrument): report the smallest delta (log points) at which the robust 95% set for the return to schooling first includes 0, and delta as a share of the replicated reduced-form coefficient. With one instrument this breakdown point equals the lower bound of the 95% interval of the reduced form; from the published conventional numbers it is about 0.045 - 1.96 x 0.018 = 0.010 for column 6 and 0.007 for column 5 (the latter matches Cinelli and Hazlett's reduced-form bound), so the replication mainly checks the robust version, and the paper states this equivalence. The Wald-based union of intervals is reported only as a secondary, non-robust comparison. As a reference scale the paper quotes Card's Table 5 direct-effect estimates (0.015 and 0.013) with the caveat that they come from the experience-endogenous, interacted-instrument model, and the direct-effect bounds of Steiner, Houssineau and Steel (2025), whose controls differ from Card's. No threshold: a breakdown point for the reader to judge.

H5 (IV vs OLS, the only test of the difference; primary Panel A column 6, column 5 alongside): a heteroskedasticity-robust control-function (Durbin-Wu-Hausman) test of the difference between the 2SLS and OLS returns, two-sided at 5%. Minimum detectable difference at 80% power, computed now from the published conventional standard errors with no data run: 2.8 x sqrt(0.055^2 - 0.004^2) = 0.154 for column 6 and 2.8 x sqrt(0.055^2 - 0.003^2) = 0.154 for column 5; the published point differences are 0.067 and 0.057, so a non-rejection is expected. The MDEs are approximations from conventional standard errors, while the test is heteroskedasticity-robust; the result is therefore reported with the robust 95% confidence interval of the IV-OLS difference (control-function coefficient), and a non-rejection is read through that interval (the differences it does not exclude), not as evidence that the two returns are equal. Under the heterogeneous-returns reading the paper adopts, a difference would compare a weighted average of returns for men whose schooling responds to proximity with an OLS coefficient, so it is reported descriptively, not as a measure of ability bias.
contribution: A logged, rerunnable replication of a canonical IV estimate of the return to schooling (already reproduced by Kling 2001 and others), with published and replicated numbers side by side and every difference explained, and a correction of the working-paper number (WP 4483, not 4832) that circulates with the data. Weak-instrument-robust inference and exclusion-restriction sensitivity on these data are already published for the specification without family background (Cinelli and Hazlett 2025: homoskedastic Anderson-Rubin set and partial-R2 sensitivity) and, with a direct-effect parameterisation, for a different control set (Steiner, Houssineau and Steel 2025). The paper adds the heteroskedasticity-robust versions on the one-endogenous-regressor specification that keeps Card's family-background controls (Panel A column 6, chosen by the crew because the weak-instrument tools need a single endogenous regressor): effective-F thresholds, the robust Anderson-Rubin set and the Conley-Hansen-Rossi breakdown point, and states that with one instrument the last two are restatements of the reduced form. In the Scout's limited search these were not reported on that column. The paper adds no new estimate of the return to schooling and interprets the IV estimate as a weighted average of returns for men whose schooling responds to proximity, not as the average return for all men.

tasks.title: Card (1994 NBER WP 4832 / 1995): the published OLS, first-stage, reduced-form and 2SLS estimates for the nearc4 specification with table, column, standard errors, N, sample rule, control set and variable construction; the data source and codebook; prior replications and reanalyses of these data (weak-IV, exclusion-restriction sensitivity, heterogeneity); and the later-literature methods named in H2-H4

question.summary: Replication of Card (WP 4483) IV return to schooling; H1 reproduction of Panel B col 6 and Panel A cols 6/5; H2-H5 weak-IV-robust and exclusion sensitivity on Panel A col 6 (col 5 alongside). Reviewer question-r2: pass, F7-F8 minor answered.
